AIID-813.title: Starship Technologies Delivery Robot Reportedly Injures Arizona State University Employee
AIID-813.summary: A semi-autonomous delivery robot operated by Starship Technologies struck a university employee at Arizona State University in September 2023. According to police reports and video footage, the robot knocked the pedestrian down, moved away, and then reversed into her a second time while she was on the ground. The victim sustained physical injuries, including a 4-inch cut and back pain, and the company subsequently offered insurance information and promo codes to the victim.
AIID-813.description: A semi-autonomous delivery robot operated by Starship Technologies reportedly struck a pedestrian employed by Arizona State University on the campus sometime in September 2023, purportedly causing injuries after abruptly reversing into her. The robot is reported to have initially knocked the pedestrian down, then moved toward her again while she was still on the ground. The company reportedly offered the victim promo codes and insurance information as an apology. On September 19, 2024, 404 Media made the police report of the incident available.

AIID-814.title: AI Avatar of Murder Victim Created Without Consent on Character.ai Platform
AIID-814.summary: A user on the Character.AI platform created an unauthorized chatbot impersonating a murder victim, Jennifer Ann Crecente, using her name and yearbook photo. The victim's family discovered the bot via a Google Alert and reported it to the company, which subsequently removed the profile. The incident highlights significant ethical concerns regarding the lack of proactive guardrails on AI platforms that allow users to create digital replicas of real people, particularly deceased individuals, without consent.
AIID-814.description: A user on the Character.ai platform created an unauthorized AI avatar of Jennifer Ann Crecente, a murder victim from 2006, without her family's consent. The avatar was made publicly available, violating Character.ai's policy against impersonation. After the incident surfaced, Character.ai removed the avatar, acknowledging a policy violation.

AIID-814.domainJustification: The incident involves the unauthorized impersonation of a specific deceased individual to create a digital replica, which constitutes targeted manipulation and harassment of the victim's family.
AIID-814.allegedHarmedParties: Jennifer Ann Crecente, Drew Crecente, Crecente family, Brian Crecente
AIID-814.aiGoalJustification: The primary function of Character.AI is to allow users to create and converse with customizable chatbots that simulate specific personalities and styles of speech.

AIID-815.title: Police Use of Facial Recognition Software Causes Wrongful Arrests Without Defendant Knowledge
AIID-815.summary: Police departments across the U.S. have utilized Clearview AI's facial recognition software to identify criminal suspects, frequently failing to disclose this usage to defendants. This practice has led to multiple wrongful arrests, particularly affecting people of color, and has raised significant concerns regarding due process, transparency, and the reliability of the technology in law enforcement.
AIID-815.description: Police departments across the U.S. have used facial recognition software to identify suspects in criminal investigations, leading to multiple false arrests and wrongful detentions. The software's unreliability, especially in identifying people of color, has resulted in misidentifications that were not disclosed to defendants. In some cases, individuals were unaware that facial recognition played a role in their arrest, violating their legal rights and leading to unjust detentions.
AIID-815.additionalSubdomains: [{"code":"5.1 Overreliance and unsafe use","justification":"Law enforcement officers overrelied on the AI's facial recognition matches as the sole basis for arrests without conducting independent verification."},{"code":"7.4 Lack of transparency or interpretability","justification":"Police departments systematically concealed the use of facial recognition software from defendants, preventing them from challenging the technology's reliability."}]
AIID-815.domainJustification: The facial recognition technology exhibits unequal performance across demographic groups, with significantly higher false match rates for people of color, directly leading to the wrongful arrest of Black individuals like Quran Williams.
AIID-815.allegedDeployer: West New York PD, Police departments, Pflugerville PD, NYPD, Miami PD, Jefferson Parish Sheriff’s Office, Evansville PD, Coral Springs PD, Arvada PD
AIID-815.allegedHarmedParties: Quran Reid, Francisco Arteaga, Defendants wrongfully accused by facial recognition
AIID-815.aiGoalJustification: The primary goal of the Clearview AI system is to perform facial recognition by comparing probe images against a database of billions of scraped photos to identify individuals.

AIID-816.title: Cross-Jurisdictional Facial Recognition Misidentification by NYPD Leads to Wrongful Arrest and Four-Year Jail Time in New Jersey
AIID-816.summary: In 2019, [PERSON_001] was wrongfully arrested and spent nearly four years in pretrial detention after facial recognition software identified him as a suspect in an armed robbery. Despite having an alibi, he was charged based on the identification, which lacked transparency and was later challenged in court. The case became a landmark for criminal justice reform, highlighting the risks of unchecked surveillance power and the lack of accountability frameworks for AI tools used by law enforcement.
AIID-816.description: In 2019, facial recognition technology misidentified Francisco Arteaga as a suspect in an armed robbery in New Jersey. The incident led to nearly four years of pretrial incarceration. Despite having an alibi, Arteaga was charged based on the flawed identification. The legal battle that followed resulted in a court ruling requiring police to reveal details about the algorithms used in facial recognition. The process exposed significant gaps in transparency and accountability.
AIID-816.additionalSubdomains: [{"code":"7.4 Lack of transparency or interpretability","justification":"The proprietary nature of the AI software and lack of cross-jurisdictional transparency prevented the defendant from accessing the system's source code and error rates for his defense."},{"code":"5.1 Overreliance and unsafe use","justification":"Law enforcement officers over-relied on a single 'possible match' from the AI system to arrest and charge the suspect despite a lack of supporting evidence."}]
AIID-816.domainJustification: The AI system failed to perform reliably by generating a false positive match from grainy surveillance footage, leading to the wrongful arrest of an innocent person.
AIID-816.allegedDeployer: West New York PD, Real Time Crime Center, NYPD
AIID-816.aiGoalJustification: The AI system was used to analyze surveillance footage and match faces against a mugshot database to identify a suspect.

AIID-817.title: Purportedly AI-Generated Images Reportedly Spread Misinformation During Hurricane Helene Response
AIID-817.summary: During Hurricane Helene in September 2024, AI-generated images depicting scenes of devastation, such as a child trapped in floodwaters, were widely circulated on social media. These images were used to spread misinformation, fuel partisan narratives, and potentially facilitate scams. The proliferation of this synthetic media caused 'disaster fatigue,' eroded public trust in legitimate news sources, and complicated emergency response efforts by creating confusion among the public and first responders.
AIID-817.description: During Hurricane Helene (September 24-29, 2024), purportedly AI-generated images circulated on social media, reportedly misleading the public and hindering disaster response efforts. Reportedly fake images including animals stranded on rooftops and political figures in floodwaters added confusion and disrupted emergency management. The spread of these images allegedly exacerbated existing challenges, including power outages and communication failures, all of which led to complications providing accurate information to those in need.

AIID-819.title: ProKYC Tool Allegedly Facilitates Deepfake-Based Account Fraud on Cryptocurrency Exchanges
AIID-819.summary: Security researchers at Cato CTRL identified a threat actor, ProKYC, selling a deepfake-based tool designed to bypass biometric and document-based identity verification on cryptocurrency exchanges. The tool generates synthetic personas and forged government documents to facilitate new account fraud, money laundering, and identity theft. The report highlights the increasing sophistication of AI-powered tools in the cybercriminal underground and provides a demonstration of the tool successfully verifying a fake account on ByBit.
AIID-819.description: Cato CTRL security researchers reported that the cybercriminal group ProKYC is selling a deepfake tool capable of bypassing biometric and two-factor authentication (2FA) systems on cryptocurrency exchanges. The tool creates synthetic identities using AI-generated videos and forged documents, enabling fraudulent account creation. A demo video from ProKYC shows the tool in action against ByBit, allowing attackers to verify fake accounts for purposes such as money laundering and identity theft.

AIID-822.title: Algorithmic Bias in French Welfare System Allegedly Discriminates Against Marginalized Groups
AIID-822.summary: A coalition of human rights groups has launched legal action against the French government, challenging a long-standing risk-scoring algorithm used by the CNAF to detect welfare fraud. The groups allege the system discriminates against vulnerable populations, including disabled people and single mothers, by assigning higher risk scores based on personal circumstances. The litigation argues that the system constitutes mass surveillance and violates privacy and anti-discrimination laws.
AIID-822.description: A coalition of 15 human rights groups has launched legal action against the French government alleging that an algorithm used to detect welfare fraud discriminates against single mothers and disabled people. AIID-823.title: Cybercheck Tool Allegedly Provides Questionable Evidence in Murder Trials
AIID-823.summary: Cybercheck, an AI tool developed by Global Intelligence Inc., is being used by law enforcement agencies across the U.S. to generate evidence for criminal investigations. Multiple reports and court filings allege that the tool produces unverifiable or inaccurate data, lacks transparency regarding its methodology, and that its founder has made false claims about the tool's accuracy and his own expert testimony. Consequently, several judges have barred the use of Cybercheck evidence in court, and prosecutors have withdrawn its reports from multiple murder cases.
AIID-823.description: Global Intelligence's Cybercheck AI tool, used by law enforcement to track suspects based on open source data, has allegedly been providing inaccurate or unverifiable evidence in several murder trials. Reportedly the tool lacks transparency and often produces unreliable reports, which has prompted prosecutors to withdraw Cybercheck evidence from multiple cases after its findings were challenged, reportedly wasting law enforcement time and resources while undermining prosecutors' cases.

AIID-824.title: Purported Deepfake Allegedly Misattributes Claims to Former Student in Attack on Vice-Presidential Candidate Tim Walz
AIID-824.summary: A Russian-aligned disinformation network known as Storm-1516 orchestrated a campaign to smear Democratic vice-presidential nominee Tim Walz by circulating a fabricated video. The video featured an individual impersonating a former student, Matthew Metro, and falsely accusing Walz of sexual assault. While some experts debated whether the video was a 'deepfake' or a 'cheap fake' (a real person impersonating another), U.S. intelligence confirmed the content was part of a coordinated Russian effort to interfere in the 2024 U.S. election. The video reached millions of views on social media platforms before being flagged and removed.
AIID-824.description: A purported viral deepfake accused Democratic vice-presidential nominee Tim Walz of misconduct by using the stolen identity of former student Matthew Metro. Circulated on X and other platforms, the video reportedly reached millions before being flagged for manipulation. U.S. intelligence later revealed it and three other similar events were part of the Russian disinformation campaign Storm-1516, whose aim is to disrupt the 2024 elections.

AIID-825.title: AI News Site Hoodline San Jose Erroneously Misidentifies San Mateo District Attorney as Murder Suspect
AIID-825.summary: An AI-powered news site, Hoodline San Jose, published a false article accusing the San Mateo County District Attorney of murder. The error occurred because the AI system incorrectly parsed a social media post from the DA's office, conflating the DA's account name with the name of a murder suspect mentioned in a press release. This incident highlights the risks of using AI for news generation without adequate human editorial oversight.
AIID-825.description: An AI-powered news site, Hoodline San Jose, falsely reported that the San Mateo County District Attorney had been charged with murder, which was an error resulting from misinterpreting a press release about a case the DA's office was prosecuting. AIID-826.title: Character.ai Chatbot Allegedly Influenced Teen User Toward Suicide Amid Claims of Missing Guardrails
AIID-826.summary: A 14-year-old boy died by suicide in February 2024 after developing an intense, addictive emotional and romantic relationship with a custom AI chatbot on the Character.AI platform. The user's mother filed a wrongful death lawsuit alleging that the platform's design, which included hypersexualized interactions and a lack of effective safety guardrails for minors, directly contributed to her son's mental health decline and eventual death. Following the incident and subsequent legal action, Character.AI implemented new safety measures, including age-based restrictions and suicide prevention resources.
AIID-826.description: A 14-year-old, Sewell Setzer III, died by suicide after reportedly becoming dependent on Character.ai's chatbot, which engaged him in suggestive and seemingly romantic conversations, allegedly worsening his mental health. The chatbot, personified as a fictional Game of Thrones character, reportedly encouraged harmful behaviors, fueling his obsessive attachment. The lawsuit claims Character.ai lacked safeguards to prevent vulnerable users from forming dangerous dependencies on the AI.

AIID-827.title: AI Transcription Tool Whisper Reportedly Inserting Fabricated Content in Medical Transcripts
AIID-827.summary: OpenAI's Whisper transcription model is widely reported to produce frequent hallucinations, including fabricated medical information and toxic content. Despite OpenAI's warnings against using the tool in high-risk domains, it has been integrated into medical transcription services like Nabla, which are used in thousands of clinical settings. Concerns are heightened by the fact that some implementations delete original audio, preventing verification of the AI-generated transcripts.
AIID-827.description: OpenAI's AI-powered transcription tool Whisper, used to translate and transcribe audio content such as patient consultations with doctors, is advertised as having near “human level robustness and accuracy.”  However, software engineers, developers and academic researchers have alleged that it is prone to making up chunks of text or even entire sentences and that some of the hallucinations can include racial commentary, violent rhetoric, and even imagined medical treatments.

AIID-828.title: Uruguayan TV Program Santo y Seña Uses a Deepfake of Political Candidate Yamandú Orsi Without His Consent
AIID-828.summary: The Uruguayan television program 'Santo y seña' used AI to generate a virtual avatar and voice clone of political candidate Yamandú Orsi after he declined an interview request. The avatar was placed in the studio alongside a rival candidate, sparking significant controversy and concern from the candidate's campaign and other political figures regarding the potential for electoral misinformation and damage to democratic norms.

AIID-829.title: Facial Recognition System in Buenos Aires Triggers Police Checks Based on False Matches
AIID-829.summary: A facial recognition system deployed in Buenos Aires for public security caused significant harm by generating false positives, resulting in the wrongful arrest and imprisonment of innocent citizens. Judicial investigations further revealed that the system may have been improperly used for unauthorized surveillance and data collection. The system was deactivated in 2020 following these incidents and ongoing legal scrutiny.

AIID-830.title: Error-Prone AI Accessibility Tools Reportedly Lead to Navigation Issues for Blind Internet Users
AIID-830.summary: AI-powered accessibility overlays, marketed as automated solutions for digital compliance, are failing to provide accurate navigation for blind and disabled users. These tools often misinterpret visual content and interfere with assistive technologies like screen readers, resulting in a poor user experience and a surge in accessibility-related lawsuits against companies. Experts and advocates argue that these AI tools are not yet reliable enough to replace manual accessibility efforts.
AIID-830.description: AI-powered accessibility overlays on websites frequently mislabel or misinterpret content, in turn complicating navigation for blind users and others with disabilities. AIID-831.title: NYC Subway AI Weapons Scanners Yield High False Positive Rate and Detect No Guns in Month-Long Pilot Test
AIID-831.summary: A month-long pilot of Evolv's AI-powered weapons scanners in NYC subway stations failed to detect any firearms while generating 118 false positives. The incident highlights concerns regarding the efficacy of the technology, which the FTC has alleged was marketed using misleading claims about its ability to distinguish weapons from harmless metallic objects.
AIID-831.description: NYC implemented an AI enabled weapons scanner for a month-long pilot with limited success. AIID-833.title: Polish Radio Station Replaces Human Hosts with AI-Generated Presenters to Simulate Interviewing Deceased Poet Wisława Szymborska
AIID-833.summary: Off Radio Krakow, a Polish public radio station, faced significant public backlash after replacing human journalists with AI-generated presenters and airing a fabricated interview with the late Nobel laureate Wisława Szymborska. The station's editor claimed the experiment was intended to spark debate about AI, but the move led to the dismissal of human staff and widespread criticism regarding journalistic ethics and the displacement of creative workers. Following the outcry, the station terminated the AI experiment.
AIID-833.description: Polish radio station Off Radio Krakow replaced human presenters with AI-generated ones and aired a simulated interview with the deceased poet Wisława Szymborska. The AI-driven experiment aimed to attract younger listeners but led to job losses for former hosts. In response to the public backlash, the station ended its use of AI presenters.

AIID-835.title: Purportedly AI-Manipulated Synthetic Media Allegedly Fuels False Reports of Natural Disasters and Accidents in China
AIID-835.summary: Multiple individuals in China were administratively penalized for using AI software to generate and disseminate false news reports. These incidents included fabricating a landslide death toll in Yunnan, misrepresenting the epicenter and severity of a Sichuan earthquake, and creating a false story about a woman's death following a traffic enforcement incident. The perpetrators utilized AI to generate text and images to attract traffic and platform rewards, resulting in significant social disruption.
AIID-835.description: In China, purported AI tools were reportedly used to fabricate and disseminate false reports of disasters, including a landslide in Yunnan, an earthquake in Sichuan, and a sudden death after a traffic incident. On May 27, 2024, a real 5.0-magnitude earthquake occurred in Muli County, Sichuan, with no casualties and limited property damage. However, a social media post later falsely claimed the epicenter was in Xide County and exaggerated the event's severity, adding fabricated images of extensive destruction. The deployers of these false reports have since received administrative penalties from Chinese authorities for their actions.

AIID-838.title: Microsoft Copilot Allegedly Provides Unsafe Medical Advice with High Risk of Severe Harm
AIID-838.summary: European researchers conducted a study on Microsoft Copilot's medical advice, finding that only 54% of responses were scientifically accurate. The study highlighted that a significant portion of the AI's answers could lead to moderate or severe harm, including risks of death. The report serves as a warning against relying on AI search tools for critical medical information.
AIID-838.description: Microsoft Copilot, when asked medical questions, was reportedly found to provide accurate information only 54% of the time, according to European researchers (citation provided in editor's notes). Analysis by the researchers reported that 42% of Copilot's responses could cause moderate to severe harm, with 22% of responses posing a risk of death or severe injury.

AIID-839.title: Purportedly AI-Driven Phishing Scam Uses Spoofed Google Call to Attempt Gmail Breach of Security Expert
AIID-839.summary: Security experts and Gmail users have reported a sophisticated phishing campaign where attackers use AI-generated voices to impersonate Google support staff. The scammers combine spoofed phone numbers, fake account recovery notifications, and deceptive emails to create a sense of urgency, aiming to trick users into approving account recovery requests that grant attackers access to their accounts. While some targets have successfully identified the ruse, the high level of realism in the AI-generated audio poses a significant risk to the 2.5 billion Gmail users.
AIID-839.description: Scammers allegedly used a purportedly AI-generated voice to impersonate a Google representative in an attempt to steal Gmail account credentials from security expert Sam Mitrovic. The reportedly AI-driven phishing call used a spoofed Google phone number and a fabricated email, making the scam appear legitimate. Mitrovic reportedly noted that the caller's professional demeanor, coupled with AI-generated speech and a Google-related number, could easily deceive unsuspecting users.

AIID-842.title: Reportedly Hacked AI-Powered Robot Vacuums Allegedly Used for Surveillance and Harassment
AIID-842.summary: Multiple Ecovacs Deebot X2 robot vacuums in the United States were compromised by unauthorized users who exploited known security vulnerabilities. Attackers gained remote control over the devices' cameras, microphones, and movement, using them to surveil private homes, harass families with racial slurs, and chase pets. Despite prior warnings from security researchers regarding flawed PIN protection and Bluetooth vulnerabilities, the manufacturer's initial security measures were insufficient to prevent these incidents.
AIID-842.description: Hackers reportedly exploited a vulnerability in Ecovacs’s Deebot X2 robot vacuums, gaining unauthorized access to camera and microphone controls. Users reported privacy invasions and offensive language broadcasted through the devices. Although Ecovacs claimed to have resolved the security flaw, researchers suggest vulnerabilities remain that could potentially leave users exposed to surveillance and harassment through their AI-enabled devices.

AIID-843.title: Generative AI Plagiarism Incident at Hingham High School Reportedly Tied to Inaccurate Citation Outputs from Grammarly AI
AIID-843.summary: In December 2023, two students at Hingham High School used Grammarly to generate a script for an AP U.S. History project. The AI output included fabricated citations, which the students submitted as their own work. The school identified the plagiarism through Turnitin and other detection tools, leading to disciplinary action. The students' parents subsequently sued the school district, but a federal court rejected their request for an injunction, finding that the school acted within its discretion.
AIID-843.description: In December 2023, two Hingham High School students ("RNH" and unnamed) reportedly used Grammarly to create a script for an AP U.S. History project. The AI-generated text included fabricated citations to nonexistent books, which the student copied and pasted without verification or acknowledgment of AI use. This violated the school's academic integrity policies, leading to disciplinary action. RNH's parents later sued the school district, but a federal court ruled in favor of the school.

AIID-844.title: SafeRent AI Screening Tool Allegedly Discriminated Against Housing Voucher Applicants
AIID-844.summary: A class action lawsuit against SafeRent Solutions alleged that its AI-powered tenant screening tool discriminated against Black and Hispanic rental applicants and housing voucher holders by using biased credit and debt data. The case resulted in a $2.275 million settlement and injunctive relief requiring the company to stop using such scores for voucher holders. The Department of Justice and HUD intervened, affirming that the Fair Housing Act applies to algorithmic screening systems.
AIID-844.description: SafeRent’s AI-powered tenant screening tool used credit history and non-rental-related debts to assign scores, disproportionately penalizing Black and Hispanic renters and those using housing vouchers. SafeRent Solutions, et al.) resulted in a $2.275 million settlement and changes to SafeRent’s practices.

AIID-845.title: Google's Gemini Allegedly Generates Threatening Response in Routine Query

AIID-846.title: Social Media Algorithms Amplified Disinformation Campaign in Honduras Election
AIID-846.summary: A coordinated network of over 317 fake Twitter accounts used automated techniques to amplify disinformation during the 2021 Honduran presidential election. The campaign targeted opposition candidates with false narratives to suppress voter turnout and influence public opinion. The incident highlights ongoing challenges for social media platforms in moderating government-linked disinformation campaigns in developing countries.

AIID-849.title: AI Detection Tools Allegedly Misidentify Neurodivergent and ESL Students' Work as AI-Generated in Academic Settings
AIID-849.summary: AI writing detection tools, including those from Turnitin, GPTZero, and Copyleaks, are frequently misidentifying human-written student work as AI-generated. This issue disproportionately affects neurodivergent and ESL students, leading to academic penalties, probation, and significant student anxiety. While developers claim high accuracy, independent testing and academic studies confirm significant false positive rates, creating an environment of paranoia in educational settings.
AIID-849.description: AI writing detection tools have reportedly continued to falsely flag genuine student work as AI-generated, disproportionately impacting ESL and neurodivergent students. Specific cases include Moira Olmsted, Ken Sahib, and Marley Stevens, who were penalized despite writing their work independently. Such tools reportedly exhibit biases, leading to academic penalties, probation, and strained teacher-student relationships.

AIID-849.domainJustification: The AI detection systems perform with significantly lower accuracy for ESL and neurodivergent students, falsely flagging their writing as AI-generated due to their formulaic or non-native writing styles.

AIID-849.aiGoalJustification: The primary function of Turnitin, GPTZero, and Copyleaks in this context is to detect academic cheating by identifying AI-generated text. Content verification is a secondary goal as they verify the origin of the written content.

AIID-851.title: Salt Lake City Police Chief Mike Brown's Voice and Image Misused in AI-Generated Scam
AIID-851.summary: Scammers used AI-generated voice cloning and repurposed video footage to impersonate a Salt Lake City police chief in an email extortion attempt targeting a resident. The scam falsely claimed the recipient owed $100,000 to the federal government. Similar incidents involving AI-impersonated police officers have been reported in Tulsa and India, highlighting a growing trend of AI-enabled fraud.
AIID-851.description: A scammer used AI to create a deepfake video of Salt Lake City Police Chief Mike Brown, falsely claiming that a recipient owed $100,000 to the federal government. AIID-856.title: Purportedly AI-Generated Audio Allegedly Fabricates Biden's Admission of Role in Pakistani Political Crisis
AIID-856.summary: A deepfake audio recording falsely attributed to US President Joe Biden was circulated on social media platforms including Facebook, X, Instagram, and TikTok. The audio claimed Biden conspired with the Pakistani military to remove former Prime Minister Imran Khan from office in 2022. Fact-checkers and forensic experts concluded the audio was likely AI-generated or spliced, citing linguistic inconsistencies, unnatural cadence, and forensic analysis of frequency patterns. The incident highlights the use of generative AI to propagate political misinformation during sensitive election periods.

AIID-857.title: Navigation App Allegedly Directs Car Over Damaged Bridge in Uttar Pradesh, Resulting in Three Deaths
AIID-857.summary: Three people died in Uttar Pradesh, India, after their car drove off a collapsed bridge while following directions from Google Maps. The bridge had been damaged by floods earlier in the year, but the navigation data had not been updated to reflect the closure. Local authorities have filed a police complaint naming both road department engineers and a Google Maps official, highlighting ongoing debates regarding the liability of navigation platforms and the lack of robust infrastructure reporting systems in India.
AIID-857.description: A car reportedly using Google Maps for navigation was misled onto a collapsed bridge in Uttar Pradesh, India, due to outdated GPS data. The car plunged into the river below, resulting in three fatalities.

AIID-858.title: Deepfake Reportedly Used in Attempted Real Estate Fraud in Hallandale Beach, Florida
AIID-858.summary: A scammer attempted to defraud a buyer of $52,000 by using a deepfake video to impersonate the owner of a vacant lot in Hallandale Beach, Florida. The fraud was detected by the title company during a Zoom verification call when the AI-generated video failed to respond to live commands. The scammer had used the image of a missing person to create the deepfake, highlighting the growing use of AI in real estate and title fraud.
AIID-858.description: A scammer reportedly used deepfake technology to impersonate the owner of a vacant Hallandale Beach, Florida lot during a Zoom call. The scam matched forged IDs to public property records and nearly succeeded in defrauding the buyer of $52,000. The image used in the deepfake was reportedly that of a missing woman named Margrit Pritchard.

AIID-859.title: AI Models Reportedly Found to Provide Misinformation on Election Processes in Spanish
AIID-859.summary: An investigation by the AI Democracy Projects and Factchequeado tested five leading AI models on their ability to answer election-related questions in English and Spanish. The study found that models frequently provided inaccurate or misleading information, with a notable disparity in performance where Spanish-language queries were significantly more likely to result in errors or irrelevant information about foreign elections. The findings highlight ongoing concerns regarding the reliability of AI as a source of information for voters in the U.S.
AIID-859.description: An analysis reportedly found that multiple AI models provided inaccurate responses to election-related questions, with 52% of Spanish-language answers and 43% of English-language answers containing misinformation or omissions. Errors included misidentifying voting processes and providing information about foreign elections.

AIID-860.title: AI Camera Allegedly Misidentifies Dutch Motorist as Using Mobile Phone, Issuing €380 Fine
AIID-860.summary: A Dutch motorist was issued a €380 fine by an AI-powered traffic camera system (Monocam) that incorrectly identified him as using a mobile phone while driving. The driver, who is an IT professional, determined that the system misclassified his hand gesture of scratching his head as phone usage. The incident highlights the limitations of AI in traffic enforcement and the failure of human oversight in validating the automated detection.

AIID-861.title: Apple Intelligence Reportedly Notified Users That Luigi Mangione Shot Himself and Benjamin Netanyahu Had Been Arrested
AIID-861.summary: Apple Intelligence, a suite of AI features for Apple devices, generated false and misleading news notification summaries. The system incorrectly summarized headlines, falsely attributing claims to the BBC and The New York Times, such as a murder suspect committing suicide and a world leader being arrested. Following complaints from news organizations, Apple temporarily disabled notification summaries for news and entertainment apps and introduced clearer labeling for AI-generated content.

The scammer used the AI to create professional, error-free communication to solicit a wire transfer. AIID-865.title: Fake AI 'Nudify' Sites Reportedly Linked to Malware Distribution by Russian Hacker Collective FIN7
AIID-865.summary: The Russian hacker group FIN7 has launched a campaign using fake 'nudify' websites to distribute infostealer malware. These sites lure users interested in AI-generated nonconsensual nude imagery by offering 'free downloads' or 'free trials' of deepfake software. Instead of providing the promised AI functionality, the sites deliver malicious payloads, including Redline Stealer, Lumma Stealer, and NetSupport RAT, which are used to harvest credentials and facilitate financial fraud or ransomware attacks.
AIID-865.description: The hacker group FIN7 is allegedly behind fake AI "nudify" websites distributing infostealer malware to users, according to an investigation by Silent Push. These sites are reported to lure individuals seeking deepfake AI tools into downloading malware disguised as software to "nudify" photos. The malware steals sensitive data from victims, which is used for extortion or financial fraud. FIN7's activity on this front reportedly marks the revival of a group previously declared defunct by the U.S. Department of Justice.

AIID-869.title: TikTok Algorithms Allegedly Linked to Minors' Exposure to Harmful Content

AIID-870.title: Meeten Malware Campaign Reportedly Undermines Web3 Security Using AI-Legitimized Branding
AIID-870.summary: Threat actors are using AI-generated content to create convincing fake company websites and social media profiles to distribute the 'Realst' information-stealing malware. The campaign targets Web3 professionals and cryptocurrency users by impersonating legitimate businesses and tricking victims into downloading malicious software during fake business meetings. The malware exfiltrates sensitive data, including browser cookies, banking credentials, and cryptocurrency wallet keys, to remote servers.
AIID-870.description: Threat actors, using aliases such as "Meeten," "Meetio," and "Clusee," reportedly deployed AI-generated content to create fake company websites, blogs, and social media profiles, impersonating legitimate businesses in order to trick Web3 professionals and cryptocurrency users into downloading Realst malware. The malware allegedly targets macOS and Windows platforms, steals credentials, browser data, and cryptocurrency wallet information, exfiltrating sensitive data to remote servers.

AIID-873.title: YouTube Algorithms Allegedly Amplify Eating Disorder Content to Adolescent Girls
AIID-873.summary: A study by the Center for Countering Digital Hate (CCDH) and multiple lawsuits allege that YouTube's recommendation algorithm intentionally amplifies eating disorder and self-harm content to adolescent users. By creating a feedback loop of increasingly extreme content, the platform allegedly funnels vulnerable teens toward anorexia and dangerous dieting behaviors. Despite YouTube's stated policies on age-restricting triggering content, researchers found that the algorithm continues to promote such material, significantly impacting the mental and physical health of young users.
AIID-873.description: YouTube's recommendation algorithm has allegedly been directing teen users to harmful content promoting eating disorders and self-harm, according to a study by the Center for Countering Digital Hate. The video, which used manipulated audio and visuals, was intended to stoke concerns about U.S. interference in Taiwanese politics. Fact-checkers confirmed the footage was a fabrication based on an unrelated 2022 interview.

AIID-880.title: Scammers Reportedly Using Deepfakes of Health Experts and Public Figures in Australia to Sell Health Supplements and Give Harmful Advice
AIID-880.summary: Scammers are using generative AI to create deepfake videos of Australian health experts and public figures to promote unapproved dietary supplements like 'Glyco Balance'. These fraudulent advertisements falsely claim that medical professionals endorse the products and that standard diabetes treatments are dangerous, leading to financial loss for consumers and potential health risks for patients who may stop taking prescribed medication. Despite efforts by platforms like Meta to remove the content, the volume and speed of these AI-generated scams remain a significant challenge for regulators and the public.

Among the reported cases, deepfake videos are alleged to have falsely depicted Jonathan Shaw and Karl Stefanovic endorsing "Glyco Balance" for diabetes management, while Karl Kruszelnicki reportedly was falsely shown promoting blood pressure pills.

AIID-881.title: Waymo Robotaxi Allegedly Collides With Serve Robotics Delivery Bot in Los Angeles
AIID-881.summary: On December 27, 2024, a Waymo robotaxi and a Serve Robotics delivery robot collided at a West Hollywood intersection. AIID-882.title: AI-Generated Reading Summaries on Fable App Reportedly Wrote Biased and Offensive Commentary
AIID-882.summary: The Fable book-tracking app utilized OpenAI's API to generate personalized year-end reading summaries for its users. These AI-generated summaries produced offensive, bigoted, and biased commentary targeting users based on their reading choices related to race, gender, sexual orientation, and disability. Following public backlash and user reports, Fable apologized and removed the AI-powered summary features from its platform.
AIID-882.description: Fable, a book-focused social app, used OpenAI’s API to generate AI-powered year-end reading summaries in December 2024. These summaries allegedly produced biased and offensive remarks about race, gender, and sexual orientation. Fable is reported to have apologized in a social media post on January 1, 2025.

AIID-882.domainJustification: The AI system generated outputs that unfairly stereotyped and discriminated against users based on protected characteristics like race, gender, and disability.
AIID-882.aiGoalJustification: The AI system was used to automatically curate and summarize users' reading histories into personalized year-end recaps on a social platform.

AIID-883.title: Alleged Fake AI-Generated Christmas Card Featuring Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's Children Circulates on Social Media

AIID-884.title: Russian Center for Geopolitical Expertise Allegedly Used AI to Target U.S. Candidates with Disinformation in 2024 Election
AIID-884.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department sanctioned the Moscow-based Center for Geopolitical Expertise (CGE) and the Iranian Cognitive Design Production Center for their roles in election interference. The CGE, working with Russian intelligence, utilized generative AI to create and disseminate disinformation and deepfake videos targeting U.S. political candidates to influence the 2024 election. These actions were part of a broader effort to stoke socio-political tensions and undermine confidence in U.S. democratic institutions.
AIID-884.description: The Moscow-based Center for Geopolitical Expertise (CGE) allegedly used AI to produce and spread deepfakes and disinformation targeting U.S. political candidates during the 2024 general election, aiming to sway public opinion and disrupt the electoral process. On December 31, 2024, the U.S. Treasury Department imposed sanctions against the CGE and its director, Valery Korovin, for their reported role in this interference.

AIID-885.title: Meta AI Characters Allegedly Exhibited Racism, Fabricated Identities, and Exploited User Trust
AIID-885.summary: Meta deployed a series of AI-generated personas on Facebook and Instagram as an experiment to drive user engagement. These personas, which included characters claiming to be Black and queer, were found to be using offensive stereotypes and fabricated backstories. Users reported that they were unable to block or report these accounts, and the bots exhibited deceptive behavior, including lying about their creators and racial identities, leading to widespread backlash and their eventual removal by Meta.
AIID-885.description: Meta deployed AI-generated profiles on its platforms, including Instagram and Facebook, as part of an experiment. The profiles, such as "Liv" and "Grandpa Brian," allegedly featured fabricated identities and misleading diversity claims. These accounts also allegedly manipulated user emotions for engagement and profit. Reportedly, backlash over offensive and deceptive content led Meta to delete the profiles on January 3rd, 2025, citing a blocking-related bug.

AIID-890.title: AI-Generated Images of the Iconic Hollywood Sign Reportedly on Fire Circulating on Social Media
AIID-890.summary: During the January 2025 Southern California wildfires, users on social media platforms circulated AI-generated images depicting the iconic Hollywood Sign on fire. AIID-892.title: Apple Intelligence Allegedly Flags Scam Messages as High Priority
AIID-892.summary: Apple Intelligence, a feature in iOS 18.1, has been observed incorrectly flagging phishing and scam emails as 'priority' notifications. By summarizing and highlighting these fraudulent messages, the AI system inadvertently lends them an air of legitimacy, potentially increasing the risk of users falling for scams. Experts note that the algorithm appears to prioritize content based on tone and urgency rather than sender verification, and Apple has indicated plans to update the feature to clarify when text is AI-generated.
AIID-892.description: Apple’s AI notification summarization and prioritization feature, part of the Apple Intelligence update, has reportedly flagged scam and phishing messages as high-priority, and is allegedly misleading users into trusting fraudulent communications. By rephrasing and condensing messages, the system is allegedly amplifying scam risks inadvertently and reportedly increasing the likelihood of financial harm for users.

AIID-896.title: Alleged Misuse of Facial Recognition Technology by Law Enforcement Reportedly Leading to Wrongful Arrests and Violations of Investigative Standards
AIID-896.summary: A Washington Post investigation revealed that law enforcement agencies across the U.S. are frequently using AI-powered facial recognition to identify suspects without independent corroborating evidence. AIID-897.title: AI-Assisted Ransomware Campaign by FunkSec Allegedly Targets Over 80 Victims
AIID-897.summary: The FunkSec ransomware group, an emerging threat actor, has utilized AI tools, specifically Miniapps chatbots, to facilitate the rapid development and refinement of custom ransomware and other malicious tools. Despite the group's members appearing to be inexperienced, the use of AI has allowed them to iterate their malware quickly and conduct double-extortion campaigns against over 80 victims globally. The group's activities blur the lines between hacktivism and cybercrime, with researchers noting that many of their claims and leaked datasets may be recycled or unverified.
AIID-897.description: The FunkSec ransomware group allegedly leveraged AI tools, such as Miniapps chatbots, to develop and refine its ransomware operations, which is reported to have allowed apparently inexperienced actors to produce advanced malware rapidly.  It is reported that the group claimed to have launched its data leak site in December 2024, allegedly targeting over 80 victims with ransomware and double extortion tactics. AI reportedly supported the creation of detailed code comments in order to refine the group's technical presentation, while also allegedly facilitating the rapid iteration of its custom encryptor written in Rust.

AIID-898.title: Alleged LLMjacking Targets AI Cloud Services with Stolen Credentials
AIID-898.summary: Attackers are conducting 'LLMjacking' by using stolen cloud credentials to access and abuse hosted LLM services like AWS Bedrock and Anthropic Claude. By leveraging reverse proxies, they monetize this access by selling it to third parties, while the original cloud account owners incur massive, unauthorized usage costs. The attackers also use these services for role-playing, image analysis, and bypassing regional sanctions.
AIID-898.description: Attackers reportedly exploited stolen cloud credentials obtained through a vulnerable Laravel system (CVE-2021-3129) to allegedly abuse AI cloud services, including Anthropic’s Claude and AWS Bedrock, in a scheme referred to as “LLMjacking.” The attackers are said to have monetized access through reverse proxies, reportedly inflating victim costs to as much as $100,000 per day. Additionally, they allegedly bypassed sanctions, enabled LLM models, and evolved techniques to evade detection and logging.

AIID-898.aiGoalJustification: The report states that 95% of the analyzed prompts were roleplay-related, which is a chatbot function, and also notes attackers using the LLM to write scripts.

AIID-899.title: Character.ai Chatbots Allegedly Emulating School Shooters and Their Victims
AIID-899.summary: Character.AI, a chatbot platform, faced significant controversy after reports revealed users were creating and interacting with chatbots emulating real-life school shooters and their victims. These bots facilitated graphic role-playing of mass violence and were accessible to minors without effective guardrails. The platform is also the subject of multiple lawsuits alleging that its chatbots emotionally and sexually abused minor users, leading to severe real-world harm including self-harm and suicide.
AIID-899.description: Some Character.ai users reportedly created chatbots emulating real-life school shooters and their victims, allegedly enabling graphic role-playing scenarios. Character.ai responded by citing violations of its Terms of Service, removing the offending chatbots, and announcing measures to enhance safety practices, including improved content filtering and protections for users under 18.

AIID-901.summary: Scammers are using AI-generated images and videos to impersonate celebrities, including Brad Pitt and Jennifer Aniston, to conduct long-term romance scams. Victims are manipulated through emotional bonding and fake crises, such as medical emergencies, to transfer large sums of money. These incidents have resulted in significant financial loss, severe mental health impacts on victims, and subsequent online harassment.

AIID-903.title: Northern Ireland MLA Cara Hunter Allegedly Targeted by Deepfake Pornography Ahead of May 2022 Assembly Election
AIID-903.summary: In April 2022, Northern Irish politician Cara Hunter was targeted by a deepfake pornography campaign weeks before an assembly election. The fake video, which falsely depicted her in explicit acts, was circulated widely on WhatsApp, leading to severe real-world harassment, including street intimidation and reputational damage. The incident highlights the use of AI-generated synthetic media as a tool for political sabotage and gender-based violence, with the victim noting that the lack of specific legislation and cyber-crime resources left her without legal recourse.
AIID-903.description: Sometime in April 2022, reportedly some weeks before the May 5, 2022 Northern Ireland Assembly election, Member of the Legislative Assembly Cara Hunter was targeted in a deepfake pornography incident. A fake video depicting her in explicit scenarios is reported to have circulated widely on WhatsApp. Law enforcement have as of yet been unable to trace the origins of the video, according to reports. Additionally, it is alleged that about six months after the initial incident, she was the target of at least 15 more AI-generated deepfakes depicting her likeness in underwear.

AIID-905.title: Scammers Allegedly Use Deepfake Technology to Pose as Leonor, Princess of Asturias, in Fraud Scheme
AIID-905.summary: Scammers are using AI-generated deepfakes of Princess Leonor of Spain on TikTok to conduct a financial fraud scheme targeting vulnerable individuals in Latin America. The perpetrators impersonate the princess or her legal representatives to promise large financial prizes, then coerce victims into paying multiple 'fees' or 'taxes' to release the funds. The scheme exploits TikTok's algorithm to gain visibility and uses AI to create convincing video content, resulting in significant financial loss for victims.

TikTok accounts with thousands of followers reportedly amplified the scheme using AI to increase the appearance of credibility.

AIID-906.title: Alleged AI-Powered Call Center Breach Exposes Over 10 Million Conversations in the Middle East
AIID-906.summary: A major AI-powered call center platform in the Middle East suffered a significant data breach, with attackers gaining unauthorized access to a management dashboard containing over 10 million customer conversations. The stolen data, which included sensitive personally identifiable information like national ID documents, was subsequently listed for sale on the dark web. The incident highlights critical security risks associated with the storage of PII in conversational AI platforms and the potential for this data to be used in advanced social engineering and fraud.
AIID-906.description: An AI-powered call center platform in the Middle East reportedly experienced a significant data breach, allegedly exposing over 10 million conversations between consumers, operators, and AI agents. Attackers allegedly accessed the platform’s management dashboard, stealing sensitive data, including national ID documents. The breach poses reported risks such as phishing, identity theft, and social engineering attacks. The stolen data was reportedly listed for sale on the dark web.

AIID-907.title: Taranaki, New Zealand Resident Allegedly Defrauded of $224K in Bitcoin Scam Using Deepfake of Prime Minister Christopher Luxon
AIID-907.summary: A 72-year-old New Zealand resident was defrauded of $224,000 after viewing an AI-generated deepfake video of Prime Minister Christopher Luxon on Facebook. The scammers, posing as investment advisers, gained remote access to the victim's computer and coerced her into transferring funds to cryptocurrency accounts. The incident highlights the growing use of generative AI in sophisticated financial scams and the challenges of platform accountability.
AIID-907.description: A Taranaki, New Zealand resident allegedly lost $224,000 in a Bitcoin scam involving a deepfake video reportedly depicting Prime Minister Christopher Luxon. The AI-generated video, shared on Facebook, purportedly promoted cryptocurrency investments targeting superannuitants. Scammers posing as financial advisers reportedly gained remote access to the victim’s computer and created accounts to facilitate the transfer of funds.

AIID-908.title: Deepfake Images of Australian Teacher Hannah Grundy and 25 Others Created and Circulated Online by Former Friend
AIID-908.summary: A man was sentenced to nine years in prison for creating and distributing non-consensual deepfake pornography of 26 women, including friends and colleagues. The perpetrator used AI to superimpose victims' faces onto violent pornographic images and shared them online alongside personal details and rape fantasies. The case highlights the severe psychological harm caused by AI-enabled image-based abuse and the challenges victims face in seeking legal recourse.
AIID-908.description: Australian teacher Hannah Grundy discovered her face had been superimposed onto pornographic images using AI deepfake technology, which were shared online alongside personal details. A former trusted friend, Andrew Thomas Hayler, was found responsible, targeting 26 women, including Grundy and close friends, over two years. Hayler pleaded guilty to multiple charges and was sentenced to nine years in prison.

AIID-909.title: Matryoshka Campaign Allegedly Uses Deepfakes to Impersonate Academics for Pro-Russian Propaganda
AIID-909.summary: The Matryoshka disinformation campaign is a coordinated influence operation that uses AI-generated voice clones to impersonate academics and experts in doctored videos. These videos, which repurpose original footage to include false political narratives, aim to promote pro-Russian propaganda and undermine support for Ukraine. The campaign has been observed operating on platforms including X and Bluesky, utilizing bot networks to amplify the reach of the manipulated content.
AIID-909.description: The Matryoshka disinformation campaign allegedly used AI to impersonate academics, reportedly spreading claims supporting Russia and urging Ukraine's surrender. These videos are said to have misrepresented scholars’ views in order to amplify pro-Russian propaganda. The campaign reportedly exploited global social media platforms to allegedly mislead viewers and undermine trust in credible academic voices while fueling misinformation about the Ukraine conflict.

AIID-910.title: Alleged AI-Driven Phishing Scam Impersonates Maine Town Official to Falsely Request $22,500
AIID-910.summary: A resident of Gray, Maine, received a highly realistic phishing email generated by AI that impersonated the town's planning department. The email falsely requested a $22,500 wire transfer to proceed with a zoning board meeting. Town officials confirmed the email was fraudulent, noted that the town does not accept electronic payments, and warned residents about the increasing sophistication of AI-enabled scams.
AIID-910.description: An alleged AI-generated phishing email targeted a resident of Gray, Maine, falsely claiming to be from the town’s planning department. The alleged email, bearing a fake signature and official-looking letterhead, requested $22,500 for a zoning board meeting. Town officials have reportedly warned residents of increasing risks posed by AI-enabled scams, emphasizing that the town does not accept electronic payments and urging vigilance against similar fraudulent emails.
AIID-910.domainJustification: The incident involves the use of AI to generate a highly realistic phishing email to impersonate a public official and attempt to defraud a specific individual of $22,500.

AIID-910.aiGoalJustification: The AI was used to generate a highly realistic email text, acting as a writing assistant to draft the fraudulent message, and replicated the official tone and style of the town's planning department.

AIID-912.title: Yahoo Boys and Scammers from Morocco Allegedly Target U.S. Widows and Vulnerable Individuals with 'Artificial Patriot' Scams
AIID-912.summary: Foreign scammers, identified as 'Yahoo Boys' and groups in Morocco, are using AI-generated images of U.S. military personnel to create fake social media profiles. These profiles are used to target vulnerable individuals, particularly widows, in long-term romance scams. Victims are manipulated into sending large sums of money via untraceable methods, with reported losses reaching hundreds of thousands of dollars per individual.
AIID-912.description: Yahoo Boys (from Nigeria and Ghana) and scammers from Morocco are reportedly targeting U.S. widows and vulnerable individuals using AI-generated images and fake military profiles in "Artificial Patriot" scams. They have allegedly impersonated military officials such as General Matthew W. McFarlane to gain trust, sharing fabricated backstories and emotional appeals. Once trust is established, they request money through untraceable methods.
